title: Future study and career plans after 4th of ESO
grammar: Will, going to, future continuous and future perfect

vocab.example: I want to get a university degree.
She is doing a summer internship.
He won a scholarship to study abroad.
I sent my job application yesterday.
She chose a career path in science.
Communication is an important skill.
Do you have the right qualifications?
My long-term goal is to become a doctor.
Vocational training is a serious option after ESO.

student.repte: Plan your future! Think about what you want to study and what career you want to pursue.

products.desc: A 150-word text outlining your future study or career plans, using future tenses correctly. You choose the text type: formal email, short essay, job application or informal email.
A 2-3 minute individual presentation on a profession you find interesting: what the job involves, the skills it needs, and how you would get there.
Use a chatbot to drill the vocabulary of your own chosen field, then bring the terms you learned back to class.

teacher.repte: Students explore future educational and professional trajectories, developing vocabulary and structures to express hypotheses and plans.
teacher.methodology: Task-Based Learning, collaborative learning, inquiry-based career research, self-regulation and peer evaluation. Letting students choose the text type makes register a deliberate decision rather than a given.
teacher.assessment: Clarity, coherence and original content; accurate range of future forms; ability to sustain a 2-3 minute talk on a self-chosen topic.

title: Migration, what if... ?
grammar: Zero, first, second, third and mixed conditionals

vocab.example: Language is one of the main migration challenges.
There are many misconceptions about immigrants.
We must fight against racism.
Classism creates social divides.
Cultural clashes can happen when adjusting to a new country.
People migrate for many different reasons.
The emotions of leaving home are complex.
They applied for asylum when they arrived.
It took them two years to settle in.

student.repte: Step into someone else's shoes. Understand the journey, challenges, and emotions of migration.

products.desc: A three-scene script and performance: 'Before Leaving', 'Once in the New Country' and 'Resolution'. Assign characters, feature all conditional types, and end with a moral and a debate.
Find a real news story about immigration, simplify it to roughly two paragraphs, list the difficult words, and write one comprehension question and one opinion question using a conditional.
Post-performance class discussion on the moral and hidden social messages of the skits.

teacher.repte: Develop empathy and social awareness regarding global migration through role-play and debate, utilizing complex conditional structures.
teacher.competencies: Ciutadana (CC1 - social identity & empathy), Llengua Estrangera 3 & 5.
teacher.methodology: Cooperative learning, dramatic role-play, empathy-focused moral discussions. Anchoring the unit in a real news story keeps an abstract topic concrete and current.
teacher.assessment: Observation of empathy, accurate use of the full conditional range, oral fluency in debate, quality of the questions written about the news story.

title: Health and Well-Being
grammar: Modals for giving advice and expressing necessity and possibility

vocab.example: Good nutrition is essential for growth.
Sleeping 8 hours is a good lifestyle habit.
Take care of your mental health as well as your body.
Regular exercise makes you stronger.
A digital detox might improve your sleep.
Always check that a health claim comes from a reliable source.
Health misinformation spreads quickly online.
A balanced diet is not the same as eating less.

student.repte: Become a wellness expert! Build a guide people actually want to read — and make sure every word of it is true.

products.desc: Narrow 'health' down to a specific niche (teen mental health, the science of sleep, digital detox...). Structure it with Question Titles the reader needs answered — 'Why am I always tired in the morning?' — never headers like 'Introduction' or 'Tips'. Use modal verbs inside every section to give advice.
Before including any fact, prove the source is credible: a medical institution, a government health site or a peer-reviewed paper. Health is sensitive — you must not spread misinformation.
A doctor-patient or coach-athlete spoken diagnostic scenario recorded for peer feedback.

teacher.repte: Promote healthy habits and metacognitive reflection on personal well-being, practicing modals of advice. The Question Title rule forces the modals to do real communicative work instead of sitting in an exercise.
teacher.competencies: Personal, social i d’aprendre a aprendre (CPSAA 5 - metacognition & habit improvement), Digital (CD1).
teacher.methodology: Project-based learning, peer-feedback loops, scenario-based role-play, explicit source-evaluation step.
teacher.assessment: Accuracy and range of modals, credibility of the sources cited, visual communication, spoken fluency.

title: Life Paths
grammar: Reported speech, tense backshifting and reporting verbs

vocab.example: Everyone has a different life path.
Overcoming personal challenges makes you resilient.
Graduating was one of her greatest achievements.
Moving abroad was the turning point in his career.
She claimed that the job had changed her completely.
He admitted he had been wrong.
They denied knowing anything about it.
Write a headline for your sixty-second news pitch.

student.repte: Discover inspiring stories around you. Interview someone whose life path inspires you and report their story back to the class.

products.desc: A short presentation supported exclusively by images. Tell the interviewee's story and reflect on how it inspires you — no text on the slides.
Choose someone accessible, write your questions first in direct speech, convert them into reported speech, then conduct the interview. Submit both columns side by side.
Turn one story from your interview into a sixty-second spoken news item, reporting what was said rather than quoting it.

teacher.repte: Practice narrative reporting and descriptive skills by synthesizing and relaying real-life inspirational interviews.
teacher.competencies: Emprenedora (CE2 - evaluating personal strengths), Llengua Estrangera 3 & 5.
teacher.methodology: Interview-based inquiry, narrative storytelling, visual presentation techniques. The news pitch compresses the same material into a timed oral format.
teacher.assessment: Correct application of reported speech backshifting and reporting verbs, oral presentation skills without text reliance.

title: Job Interview
grammar: Question formation, indirect polite questions and professional register

vocab.example: I saw several job advertisements online.
A good cover letter is essential.
Follow standard CV conventions.
Use action verbs like 'managed' or 'created' in your CV.
The advert lists the main duties of the post.
The compensation includes a bonus structure.
We interviewed six candidates.
They decided to hire her after the second interview.

student.repte: Get ready for the real world! Build the job market first, then apply to it and survive the interview.

products.desc: Publish a job offer as a PDF. Include the company description; the job title, department, duties and reporting manager; base salary or hourly rate, pay frequency and any bonus; and the start logistics.
Choose two of your classmates' job offers and apply: one modern CV plus a cover letter tailored to each post.
Recruiters interview the candidates and record it. Rehearse pronunciation and intonation first — polite indirect questions throughout.

teacher.repte: Simulate a professional recruitment cycle focusing on formal register, direct questioning, and active listening.
teacher.competencies: Llengua Estrangera 3.4 (discourse strategies, turn-taking, managing communication challenges).
teacher.methodology: Simulation and role-play, peer recruitment, formal writing practice. Splitting the project into a numbered two-part sequence means the class writes the job market before applying to it, so every application has a real counterpart.
teacher.assessment: Formality of register, accuracy in question formation, completeness of the job-offer specification, interaction strategies under pressure.

vocab.example: Detectives use deductive reasoning to solve cases.
The area was secured with crime scene tape.
They found several clues in the room.
The fingerprints are crucial evidence.
They created suspect profiles based on the testimonies.
The suspect whose alibi failed became the prime suspect.
The witness who saw the car came forward.
Nobody could establish a motive.

student.repte: Become a detective! Invent a crime mystery and challenge your classmates to solve it using clues.

products.desc: A single presentation slide displaying twelve picture-only clues with absolutely no text.
A short narrative connecting all clues using accurate relative clauses and identifying the culprit.
An interactive classroom round where the team projects their clue board and fields classmates' questions.

teacher.repte: Consolidate the year's grammar (questions, reported speech, modals) through a capstone deductive reasoning project. NOTE: delivered in full in 2024-25, but not reached in 2025-26 — the year ended on unit 5.
teacher.assessment: Mastery of relative clauses, ability to field unscripted questions, narrative cohesion.
